quote: three more at the stake line have bows
why: Round 7 said 'Two hobgoblins stand guard over the line with bows.' The count of archers changes with no explanation.

quote: thumb tucked in, in the clan sign for
why: Wren is a herder's daughter from another family (Pell Harrow-side), yet she makes 'the clan sign' of Korvash's clan. Round 14 has Korvash use it back as if it were a shared signal.

quote: the high road north is a day and a half away at a forced pace, or two at an ordinary one
why: Round 1 and round 3 make the Goat's Throat 'a night's hard march' (7 hours). Round 24 has Korvash reach the Throat in about 8 hours.

quote: I have walked those rocks for two seasons to keep them off
why: Round 12 (Ushk) and round 17 (Gorrak) say the hooded figure was seen 'two moons' ago, 'two moons, no more'. Two seasons is several times longer.

quote: You have kept your word to the Tallies for eleven days of a year and a day
why: The oath was sworn on Day 2 and this is Day 16, so fourteen days.

quote: I couldn't even climb to the cairn.
why: Tessa left the horn goat, the ribbon, the 'Not yet' scratch and the slate chip at or near the cairn (rounds 11, 24, 26). She also says 'Gorrak's man saw me go', but in round 25 Gorrak says he himself saw her and 'did not raise my hand'. Round 23 has a hooded girl delivering cheese near Harrowmere while she says she has been a mender at Greyshaft since autumn.

quote: He keeps all the keys in his lap.
why: Tessa said in round 39 'The door key's on the Foreman's chain.' Hask's ring then opens the door and the manacle (rounds 49 and 53).

quote: forty small faces are turned toward you
why: Round 45 and round 49 give ninety-odd or ninety-four children in the Row; round 49 also says 'forty children flinch'.

quote: the wrong shoulders on a man in a Warden's cloak
why: In round 50 Korvash took 'a guard's cloak', not Warden Hask's.

quote: Harrowmere is three days' march for children on foot.
why: Greyshaft is 'three days' road' from the Goat's Throat for an adult at a hard pace (rounds 25, 26, 29), and Harrowmere is a further night's march past the Throat. For small children it should be well over three days.

quote: There's no oil flask on your belt, only your torches and tinderbox.
why: Round 45 says his belt was taken from him. Round 59 then puts the key ring and horn charm 'on your belt'.

quote: Vael will be on this road by dusk, and he can fetch you himself.
why: Cinder Ford and the Throat are three days' road from Greyshaft, the alarm rang under an hour earlier, and the scout says a rider has 'already' gone. Gorrak could not be on this road the same day.

quote: the key ring and Dargan's carved horn charm are both still on your belt
why: The horn charm hangs on a thong around his neck/chest (rounds 3, 7). His belt was taken in round 45, so the key ring cannot be 'on your belt' either.

quote: Greyshaft is a night's march away
why: Round 63 ended with 'Greyshaft is three days' road, and midwinter's eve is tomorrow'. Round 64 makes it a night's march (arrival 'at dusk tomorrow'), with no explanation for the shortcut changing the distance.

quote: Six of the seven hobgoblins in the room hear only a prisoner talking to his goats
why: In round 73 the singed-beard guard (one of the six in this room, round 76) says in Goblin: 'Sick men don't mutter in Draconic about goats.' He understood Draconic. Round 80's dice note says 'none of the room speaks Draconic'.

quote: My rider is still waiting at the Stones for a word from me.
why: Round 77: 'I have a rider who can be at the Stones in one [day]. I would prefer not to send him.' Rounds 78-82 treat the rider as not yet sent and to be recalled. Round 81 puts him already waiting at the Stones.

quote: She snatched the lamp off the desk and hurled it
why: In round 80 the Foreman slid the lamp 'past the ledger and out of her reach, to stand at his own elbow' with a spear behind Tessa. Here she simply takes it off the desk. The player's own plan (table toppling lamp, pen and ledger onto the Foreman) is also replaced without comment.

quote: a finger or two from the spear that lies slack across it
why: Round 82 says the spear was taken from Tessa's knees ('with the spear withdrawn from her knees'). Round 83 puts it across her knee again.

quote: The sixth hangs back with his sword half drawn, not choosing.
why: The dice show Guard 6 attacking Grey-eyes ('Guard 6 longsword vs Guard Grey-eyes (AC 18)'), and round 85 calls Guard 6 one of 'the ones who never wavered'.

quote: Three of the guards freeze where they stand.
why: A few paragraphs later the same reply says 'Guards 3, 4 and 6, the ones who never wavered, are turning on Tessa' and the fifth has backed to the wall. The frozen three and the 'never wavered' three cannot both be right.
